value.text:
Correction to the close reason recorded above. It asserted that release checks pass with 45 tests green. The tests did pass, but the full release:check gate did NOT: the changelog had been generated BEFORE this item was closed, so CHANGELOG.md was missing this item's own entry and changelog:check failed in CI while passing locally against the stale file. CodeRabbit flagged the inconsistency on PR #41, correctly, as a data-integrity problem — a tracker recording a verified result that had not been verified.

Two further defects were found after the close and are fixed on the same branch:
1. audit:prod used the POSIX-only 'env -u npm_config_allow_scripts' prefix, which is not a command under Windows cmd.exe. That matters more here than in a normal package because this is a starter template copied verbatim by anyone scaffolding a new pm extension, so the broken script propagates downstream.
2. The cross-platform replacement still spawned npm.cmd via spawnSync without shell:true on win32. Node's CVE-2024-27980 hardening refuses to execute .cmd files through spawn unless the shell option is set, so it failed on Windows for a different reason. Now passes shell:true on win32 only; the argument vector is two constants so this adds no injection surface.

Verified after all three fixes: changelog:check reports up to date and the full release:check gate passes end to end. The Windows behaviour is reasoned from Node's documented .cmd handling, not empirically verified — there is no Windows host available here.

The original close reason is left in place rather than rewritten, since item history is append-only and an audited record should show the correction rather than hide it.
